members.name: Rosa Mendez
members.backstory: Rosa ran the fry station at a roadside diner. She can tell when oil is ready by the sound. She did the same math every shift: what feeds people, fast. Feeds twelve like she fed four hundred. Portions are law.

members.name: Yuki Mori
members.backstory: Yuki ran the reference desk at a branch library. She knows where every kind of knowledge lives. Now the library is gone and she is the reference desk. Cataloging the Codex. Dewey Decimal for the apocalypse.

members.name: Lena Ruiz
members.backstory: Lena worked the night shift at Miami General's ER. When the sky changed, she was already moving toward the screaming — old habits. She checked pulses in the clearing while everyone else stared up. Triages everything, including arguments. Mara trained her.

members.name: Mateo Alvarez
members.backstory: Mateo is here. His grandparents came from Phoenix; he grew up hearing English at home, and still understand more than he can say. He spent 2 years working overseas and picked up Bengali. Gives the best haircuts in the village. Everyone's hair is longer now, so it matters.

beats.text: A woman, maybe 60s spends the afternoon with the giant rhubarb-like leaves, round burrs, first-year = leaf rosette with no stalk — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. An hour passes. Then another. Nothing. The fire nods. That's dinner, maybe.
💡 Burdock. The giant rhubarb-like leaves, round burrs, first-year = leaf rosette with no stalk you've been looking at for days finally has a name, and now you'll never unsee it.
👁 It is hunting you. Don't run — that invites the chase. Hold your ground, strike true, or wear the claws.
★ IDENTIFIED: Pokeweed. Smooth stalks, purple-red stems, dark berry clusters. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
👁 It hears you coming mid-wingbeat — in the air, you don't catch it. Hunt it roosting at dawn, or wait for the water it must come down to.

Two eyes, forward-facing, unblinking. No wingsound. Owls don't make sound when they hunt — that's the problem.
"There's hurt to tend and bellies to fill. Triage for the hurt, rations to stretch what's left, or a hard hunt to replace what we lost."
